skill.name: slide-making-skill
skill.description: Build native PowerPoint slide pages with PptxGenJS, including layout dimensions, text, images, charts, theme rules, and preview export guidance.
skill.summary: Generate single-slide PowerPoint pages with PptxGenJS rules and QA checks.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: Static findings were documentation examples and markdown formatting, not malicious execution or exfiltration. The only net new concern is global npm install guidance in pptxgenjs.md, which can modify a user environment and should be constrained. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent found.

remediation.issue: Global npm install guidance modifies the user environment.
remediation.suggestion: Use project-local dependencies, pin package versions, and ask for user confirmation before installing packages.

remediation.issue: Remote image URL examples may encourage network-dependent slide assets.
remediation.suggestion: State that example.com values are placeholders and prefer local or base64 assets for generated slides.

remediation.issue: QA commands assume local command-line tools are available.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users before running markitdown or grep, and explain that commands operate only on generated preview files.

semantic_findings.title: Global Package Installation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: pptxgenjs.md recommends `npm install -g react-icons react react-dom sharp`. A global install changes the user environment and pulls packages from the network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and cites global npm installation. It appears useful for icon rendering, but it still expands supply-chain and environment-modification risk.

content.value_statement: Building native PowerPoint slides by hand can be slow and inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code precise PptxGenJS rules for slide layout, styling, and QA.
actual_capabilities: Provides PptxGenJS guidance for text, shapes, images, icons, charts, tables, and backgrounds.
Defines font, color palette, page badge, and theme object rules for consistent slides.
Specifies a synchronous createSlide(pres, theme) format for single-slide JavaScript files.
Shows preview export patterns for native PowerPoint files.
Includes QA steps for text extraction and placeholder checks.
limitations: Focuses on single-slide JavaScript files, not complete deck orchestration.
Requires PptxGenJS and related Node packages in the user environment.
Does not provide image assets or external data sources.
Requires manual visual review to confirm final slide quality.

use_cases.title: Create a Branded Slide
use_cases.description: Turn a short brief and color palette into one native PowerPoint slide.

use_cases.title: Fix PptxGenJS Output
use_cases.description: Review a slide file for layout, theme, font, and export problems.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Data Slide
use_cases.description: Build a chart or table slide with consistent styling and readable labels.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Cover Slide
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one simple slide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use slide-making-skill to create a cover slide. Use this title, subtitle, slide number, and color palette: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Chart Slide
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one PptxGenJS slide from this dataset. Use a clean chart, readable labels, and the provided theme colors: [data].

prompt_templates.title: Repair an Existing Slide
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a current file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PptxGenJS slide against the skill rules. Identify issues, then provide a corrected single-slide implementation: [file].

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Complex Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one native PowerPoint slide from this wireframe. Include text hierarchy, image placeholders, chart styling, alt text, and QA steps: [brief].

output_examples.input: Create a cover slide for a quarterly review with a blue and green palette.
output_examples.output: A single-slide implementation plan with centered title, subtitle, approved fonts, palette background, and preview export guidance.

output_examples.input: Fix a slide where text wraps badly and colors do not match the theme.
output_examples.output: A corrected slide structure with shrink-to-fit title handling, theme keys, normal body text, and QA checks.

output_examples.input: Build a sales chart slide from quarterly revenue numbers.
output_examples.output: A chart slide design with labeled axes, muted gridlines, data labels, palette-based colors, and page number badge placement.

best_practices: Provide palette values, slide number, layout, and copy before asking for a slide.
Render a preview and run text extraction before approving the slide.
Keep body text normal weight and reserve bold style for headings.
anti_patterns: Using colors outside the provided palette or hex values with #.
Adding async slide builders that the compile script cannot await.
Declaring success before rendering and fixing at least one issue.

faq.question: Can this skill create a full presentation deck?
faq.answer: It focuses on one slide file at a time. Deck assembly requires separate orchestration.

faq.question: Does it require PptxGenJS?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for native PowerPoint generation with PptxGenJS.

faq.question: Can it use custom fonts?
faq.answer: It recommends Arial for English and Microsoft YaHei for Chinese. Other fonts need user approval.

faq.question: Can it add charts and tables?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference covers common chart types, tables, labels, colors, and layout options.

faq.question: Does it support remote images?
faq.answer: The reference shows URL examples, but local or base64 assets are safer for reliable output.

faq.question: How should output be checked?
faq.answer: Render a preview, extract text, search for placeholders, fix issues, and verify again.
